minutes.headline: Committee voted to rebid the bus contract instead of extending DBus a fourth year, and took no action on the pesticides bill.
minutes.summary: Hybrid meeting with one member on Zoom. Back-to-school reports, capital plan, athletics, personnel and a transportation rebid were taken. Votes covered a line-item transfer, a police body camera policy and SRO MOU, a trumpet donation, two policies, and no action on the pesticides bill. Committee reports covered the TC Passios renovation estimate and the finance committee.

public_comment.topic: Chair called for public comment on agenda items; none offered.
Teachers' association representative gave a back-to-school update, thanked administration, and noted heat concerns at the primary school and Turkey Hill.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to authorize administration to rebid the transportation contract rather than exercise the fourth contract year.
The committee took no action on the Massachusetts School Children Pesticides Act, H926; the vote count was not audible.
The committee accepted the FY22 budget update as a report in progress, after approving a textbook-to-phonics line item transfer.
The committee accepted the police body-worn camera policy and SRO MOU, a trumpet donation, and policies 3201 and 3203.01, each by roll call.
The TC Passios renovation estimate was reported as high, and a teardown and new-build estimate is being prepared.

why_it_matters: The bus contract goes out to bid, so the district's transportation price for FY23 will be set by new bids rather than by a fourth-year extension, and DBus's proposed increase was called very high compared with other districts.
The TC Passios estimate and the primary school air conditioning project could become future capital requests that residents are asked to vote on.
watch_next: Rebid timing and parameters for the transportation contract, expected in the next months.
The committee's discussion of an opinion on a new town building near the schools at the next meeting.
